collection.description: A traveller has laid out a long cloth on the grass by the meeting hut, and on it, in rows, are masks.

ask.text:
A traveller has laid out a long cloth on the grass by the meeting hut, and on it, in rows, are masks. Dozens of them, carved from wood and painted in every colour: bird faces with long beaks, fish faces with round staring eyes, laughing faces, sleepy faces, cross faces, faces nobody can quite describe. Bright ribbons tied to the corners of the cloth flutter in the wind.
A crowd has gathered in no time. "Try one," the seller says, smiling, to anyone who comes close. "Go on. Anyone can be anything, for a little while." The masks were carved from a lightning-struck tree on the seller's home island, the seller says, "and lightning always leaves a little of itself behind."
(Name) has been standing at the front for a long time, trying to decide. Two of them keep catching (his/her) eye: a bird mask with blue and green feathers, and a big, round, painted laughing face. Which one should (he/she) try?

c1o1.text: (Name) loves it. (He/She) loves it so much that (he/she) can't take it off. (He/She) runs home and comes back with (his/her) very best basket, the one (his/her) grandmother made, and trades it on the spot. From then on, (name) wears the bird mask to every festival, and sews feathers to match onto (his/her) clothes, and dances with (his/her) arms out like wings. The children call (him/her) "the bird." (Name) doesn't mind one bit.

c1o2.text: The moment the mask is on, (name) opens (his/her) mouth to say something, and what comes out is: "CAW." (He/She) tries again. "Kreeee." And again. "Hoo hoo." (He/She) can't stop making bird noises. Not one word comes out but squawks and whistles and trills. The children are absolutely delighted, and start making bird noises back. (Name) is not delighted at all, and tears the mask off, and the words come back. The seller laughs and laughs and puts the bird mask away under the cloth.

c1.text: The seller lifts the bird mask and ties it on (name)'s face with a soft cord. It's light as a leaf. The feathers brush (his/her) cheeks. Through the eye holes the world looks somehow higher, and brighter, and very far away...

c2o1.text: (Name) laughs for an hour. (He/She) can't stop. (He/She) laughs at the crowd, at the sky, at (his/her) own feet, at the very idea of feet. (He/She) lies on the grass holding (his/her) sides, laughing, and soon everyone watching is laughing too, without knowing why. When the seller finally unties the mask, (name) lies there panting, with tears on (his/her) face. And (he/she) feels lighter than (he/she) has in years. Something (he/she) has carried around for a long time, some old grudge, has simply been laughed away.

c2o2.text: (Name) looks at (himself/herself) in the seller's bronze mirror, the big laughing face looking back. Somehow it fits. The seller watches (him/her), head on one side. Then the seller waves a hand. "Keep it," the seller says. "It suits you." (Name) tries to give it back, tries to pay, but the seller won't hear of it. It really does suit (him/her). (Name) starts painting (his/her) own face to match on festival days, with bright colours and a big painted smile, and the whole village learns to look forward to it.

c2.text: The seller ties on the big round laughing face. It's heavy and warm, and smells of old wood and paint. For a moment nothing happens. Then (name) feels a giggle coming up from somewhere very deep...
